recognize_zh: 周邊血液抹片中央有一個顆粒性白血球，細胞質內充滿粗大、深紫黑色的顆粒並覆蓋在分葉核上；單看此圖極像嗜鹼性球，需結合注射碘造影劑後採檢的病史，才能判讀為嗜中性球內的黑色色素（contrast-associated pigment）。
features: Single granulocyte about 1.5 times red cell diameter
Cytoplasm densely packed with coarse, irregular dark purple-black granules
Granules overlie and partly obscure a lobulated nucleus; faint pink cytoplasm between granules
Background red cells with several echinocytes (crenated cells)
Few scattered platelets; no other leukocytes in field
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a single granulocyte whose cytoplasm is packed with coarse, irregular dark purple-black granular material that overlies and partially obscures a lobulated nucleus. The surrounding red cells are normochromic with several echinocytes, and scattered platelets are present. In isolation, the cell closely resembles a basophil or a neutrophil with heavy toxic granulation; the reported history of blood drawn after iodinated contrast injection, with similar black material in other neutrophils and myeloid precursors, supports interpretation as ingested pigment. Findings are suggestive of contrast-associated pigment in a neutrophil, with toxic changes in a septic patient.

ddx.vs: Basophil granules are uniformly purple-black and water-soluble, while pigment-laden neutrophils show similar material in bands and myelocytes in the same smear and a neutrophil-type pink cytoplasm between granules.
Toxic granules are fine to coarse dark azurophilic granules that do not typically pack the cytoplasm as black clumps obscuring the nucleus.
Large dark granules are present in all neutrophils as a constitutional finding (mucopolysaccharidoses), independent of contrast exposure.
Hemozoin appears as brown-black refractile clumps, usually with parasitized red cells in the smear.
